topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the students and outlines the core aims and comparative learning outcomes of the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional Modalities and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional cancer treatments—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapeutic agents—along with their systemic toxicities and efflux-mediated drug resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities and Repair Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on therapeutic strategies designed to exploit specific cancer cell weaknesses, such as hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint failures, and synthetic lethality in DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogene Addiction and Kinase Inhibitor Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how hyperactivated driver kinases are targeted based on oncogene addiction, as well as the structural and bypass resistance mechanisms that emerge during treatment.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the design and therapeutic application of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates directed against tumor-associated surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell Exploitation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the concepts and clinical modalities used to harness and re-engineer the host immune response against tumors, including checkpoint inhibitors, BiTEs, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Challenges, Long-Term Progress, and Future Directions in Cancer Therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the historical progress, persistent clinical challenges, future perspectives, and ethical dilemmas surrounding cancer treatment paradigms.
